title: openai-compat: tool_choice semantics + schema mapping + tool message formatting (streaming safe)
author: Priya Raman
description: Motivation: align Redwood's OpenAI-compatibility layer with the de-facto tool/function calling semantics (tool_choice + function_call) while making streaming stable for tool execution flows. This PR implements three related pieces: 1) tool schema mapping: map OpenAI function/tool JSON Schema definitions to Redwood's internal tool input validators so that calls are validated consistently across hosted/dedicated/private deployments; 2) tool_choice semantics: accept and emit tool_choice structured responses from models that indicate intent to call one of the registered tools (name + arguments), and map to internal call execution or fallback policies; 3) tool message formatting: standardize how tool invocations and tool outputs are represented in the assistant/chat message stream so that streaming responses remain stable when a model decides to call a tool mid-stream. Changes are backwards compatible with existing OpenAI-compat routes; default behavior remains unchanged unless the request uses the new tool_choice or schema mapping flags. Checklist: - [x] schema parsing + validator generation for tools - [x] tool_choice -> execution routing + policies - [x] streaming chunking for tool invocation markers - [x] SDK compatibility knobs (Python/TS) - [x] docs and migration note - [x] unit + integration tests (runtime + e2e) Backwards compatibility & migration notes: - Existing customers who do not enable OpenAI-compatible tool semantics will see no behavior change. - Customers using the older function_call compatibility should be able to flip a flag to get tool_choice semantics; migration docs included. - Streaming tool invocation now emits a deterministic event sequence (assistant.pre_tool_call, tool.call_stream, tool.finish, assistant.post_tool_call) to ensure SDKs can surface a smooth streaming UX. Testing: unit tests added for schema->validator generation, integration tests for tool execution via sandbox model, end-to-end test that exercises streaming tool calls through the hosted API. Performance: negligible impact on median latency for non-tool calls; slight overhead (~2-5ms) when validating large schema inputs in the hot path. Rollout plan: staggered rollout behind feature flag, start with internal Canary orgs, then beta opt-in customers, then GA. Related: ENG-4452 (tooling semantics), ENG-4498 (streaming stability).
